D013-D020_h001.question:
I’ve just been… off since last fall. Some days, I barely make it through my shift. I work nights now—one of the line machines—and normally I can push through, but lately, even reaching for a part or tossing a defective piece feels like my arms are full of cement. I don’t walk fast like I used to. Supervisors haven’t said anything, but I know they’ve noticed.

And the crying—it just comes. I’ll be standing there, scanning parts, and suddenly I’m tearing up. No real reason. Sometimes I think… I don’t know, maybe the plant shutting down years ago, the one where my mom worked—that was my fault. Like, if I’d done something different, maybe they wouldn’t have cut jobs. I know that doesn’t make sense, but it sits on me.

I don’t want to hurt myself, but... I do wish I wouldn’t wake up some mornings. That it’d just be over. 

There’s been stress—my landlord wants to sell, money’s tight, but I can’t point to one thing and say, “That’s why I fell apart.” It’s like the sadness just… settled in.
D013-D020_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h001.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling… hollow, for about five months now. It’s like there’s just nothing inside—no joy, no sadness, not even worry. I used to find peace in designing, sketching pieces late into the night, but now I can’t even lift my hand to pick up my tools without it feeling like a chore. I walk slower, I talk slower—I notice it when I’m trying to meet a client, and they’re waiting for me to respond, but the words just won’t come quickly.

Little things weigh on me. I spilled coffee last week and stood there staring at the mess, thinking I didn’t deserve to have nice things, that I ruin everything. That sounds silly, but it felt true in the moment. Sometimes, when I’m on the balcony of my studio, I get this sudden lurch—a rush to step forward. No plan, no desire to die, just… a pull. It frightens me.

I don’t know if it’s because my ex and I finalized the divorce last winter, or just life. Some days I think I should be over it by now. Other days, I wonder if I’ll ever feel like myself again.
D013-D020_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h002.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h003.question:
I’ve just been feeling… hollow, like nothing really matters or connects anymore. It’s been this way for about five months, maybe a bit more. I used to love being in the kitchen—planning dishes, tasting, even the chaos of service—but now I stand there in my uniform, and it’s like I’m watching someone else move. I don’t feel sad, exactly. Just… empty.  

I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. In class, I’m constantly picking at the skin around my nails or pacing between stations when I should be prepping. My instructor noticed and asked if I’m okay, but I don’t know how to explain it. I keep thinking I’m messing up more than I should—like burning a sauce means I’m failing everyone, and that I *deserve* to fail. It feels stupid when I say it out loud, but it sits on me.  

Sometimes, I catch myself thinking, “I just want to disappear,” or “What’s the point?” Not with a plan or anything—just a constant hum in the back of my head.  

A lot has changed since I moved for school. I don’t have my usual people around. But I can’t tell if that’s why I feel like this… or if it would’ve happened anyway.
D013-D020_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h003.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h004.question:
I’ve been off since around spring—about five months now, maybe a bit less. It started creeping in after we lost a kid in that house fire downtown. I keep thinking about it… not just the call, but little things, like whether I should’ve forced entry sooner, or if I missed a sign. I know logically it wasn’t on me, but it feels like it was. I beat myself up over small stuff too—like forgetting to take out the trash or snapping at my wife. I feel like I should be punished, like I don’t deserve to be okay.

I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. I pace at night, pick at my hands until they’re raw. My wife says I’m like a wire—tense all the time. Emotionally? I don’t feel much. Not sadness, not joy. It’s like I’m watching life through glass. I catch myself wishing I wouldn’t wake up, not because I want to end things, but because the weight feels endless.

Work’s harder—I push through, but I’m not present. I don’t know if this is grief, stress, or something more. It’s been tough, but I can’t say exactly when it crossed a line.
D013-D020_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h004.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h005.question: I’ve just been crying all the time—sometimes for no real reason, other times it’s little things, like spilling coffee or missing a deadline at work. It feels like I can’t keep myself together. My husband says I’ve changed—like I’m distant, slower to respond, even over dinner. I notice it too; I’ll get asked a simple question and it takes me forever to form the words. I keep going over things I’ve said at meetings, tiny mistakes I made in code months ago, things no one even noticed. I beat myself up about them constantly, like I should’ve been better. Five months ago, after a particularly rough week, I took a bottle of pills… not enough to actually do it, I think, but enough that I knew I shouldn’t have them around. I didn’t tell anyone until my husband found them. Work’s getting harder—meetings feel exhausting, and I’ve had to ask for extensions. I don’t know if it’s from what’s been going on with my mom’s illness or just… something deeper. It’s all blurred together now.
D013-D020_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D013-D020_h005.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h006.question:
I’ve just been feeling so down… like a heavy cloud won’t lift. It’s been like this for about two months now—just this constant sadness that doesn’t seem to go away, no matter what I do. I wake up after eight hours of sleep, but I still feel exhausted, like I didn’t rest at all. Some days, even deciding what to wear or what to eat feels overwhelming. I keep second-guessing myself, and simple choices take forever. 

I work from home tutoring high school students, and lately I’ve had to reschedule sessions because I just can’t focus or find the energy. It’s starting to affect my income, which makes me more anxious. There are times—more often than I’d like to admit—when I think maybe I wouldn’t mind if I didn’t wake up. Nothing specific, just… I don’t feel like I’m getting anything right anymore. 

A few things have been tough lately—my ex-husband moved out of state with our son, and I’ve been on my own. I don’t know if it’s that, or if it’s something deeper, or just life piling up. I can’t tell what’s causing what anymore. Everything just feels… stuck.
D013-D020_h006.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D013-D020_h006.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling really down for about two months now—just this heavy, constant sadness that doesn’t go away, even when I’m teaching. It’s strange because I love my work, but lately, it feels like I’m going through the motions. I wake up after a full night’s sleep and still feel exhausted, like my body’s weighted down. My clients have started to notice I seem quieter, less present.  

Making even small choices has become overwhelming. I’ll stand in front of my closet and freeze, unsure what to wear—something I never struggled with before. Same with picking meals. It’s not just preference—it feels like my mind shuts down.  

There are times, especially at night, when I think, “I don’t want to be here anymore,” or “What’s the point?” It’s not that I’d ever act on it, but the thoughts just keep coming.  

I went through a really tough breakup right before this started—my divorce finalized last year, but this was different, more intense. Still, I can’t tell if I’m just struggling to adjust or if it’s something deeper. I function—teach my classes, pay bills—but it takes everything out of me.
D013-D020_h007.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D013-D020_h007.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h008.question:
I’ve been working the night shift at a corner store for about a year now—mostly quiet, but it gets to you after a while. Lately, I just feel… empty. Like I’m moving through everything, but nothing really touches me. It’s been like this for maybe two months. I don’t get excited about things I used to, not even the little stuff. I didn’t used to be this way.

Sleep’s been bad. I keep having the same dream—something about being trapped, walls closing in. I wake up sweating, heart racing. Sometimes I don’t even want to fall back asleep. I’ve missed shifts because I overslept or just couldn’t get up, and my manager’s starting to notice.

I’ve been forgetting things—where I put the cleaning supplies, whether I locked the back door. My mind feels foggy, like I’m not present. A few weeks ago, I took a bunch of painkillers. Not sure I wanted to die, but I didn’t care either. I didn’t tell anyone.

There was some stuff going on—my dad got sick, money’s tight—but I don’t know if that’s really why. It just feels like everything turned gray.
D013-D020_h008.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D013-D020_h008.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h009.question:
I’ve just turned 23, and honestly, the last couple of months have been… really hard. I wake up in the middle of the night, sometimes multiple times, and just lie there. It’s like my brain won’t shut off—going over everything I’ve messed up, how I’m not working, how I keep getting rejected from jobs. I cry a lot, more than I ever used to. It’s embarrassing, but sometimes I’ll just start tearing up while watching something simple, or even in the shower.

Focusing on anything feels impossible. I’ll try to read a paragraph or follow along in a video, but my mind drifts, and I have to reread it five times. I’ve missed a few check-ins with people who were helping me look for work—just couldn’t bring myself to answer.

About six weeks ago… I took a bunch of old painkillers. I didn’t tell anyone until afterward. It wasn’t planned exactly, just felt like too much. Things have been off since my dad lost his job last year—our family’s been struggling, and I feel like I should be doing more, but I can’t even take care of myself right now.

I don’t know if this is just stress or something deeper. Some days I think I’ll snap out of it, but then it drags on.
D013-D020_h009.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D013-D020_h009.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling… off for about two months now. Some days, it’s like a heaviness just sits in my chest when I wake up—sometimes as early as 4 a.m. I lie there, staring at the ceiling, unable to fall back asleep, thinking about how tired I am but also how pointless it feels to get up. My studio’s been quiet. I used to lose myself in designing pieces, sketching, setting stones—now I can’t even focus long enough to finish a simple wire wrap. My mind feels foggy, like I’m underwater, trying to grab thoughts before they float away.

I’ve had a lot on my mind since the divorce finalized—lonelier than I thought I’d be. Money’s tight with the studio rent and fewer commissions coming in. There are moments, late at night, when I think, “What’s the point? I’d just rather not be here.” But I don’t plan anything—I just feel numb, stuck.

I’m still going to work, forcing myself, but I’m not producing much. I cancel appointments. I avoid friends. I know I should care more, but it’s hard to summon anything. I wonder if this is just grief… or if it’s becoming something worse. I don’t know where the sadness stops and something clinical begins.
D013-D020_h010.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Specific Phobia
D013-D020_h010.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h011.question:
I’ve been running my restaurant for over fifteen years, and lately, I just feel… hollow. It’s like there’s a space inside me that nothing fills—not the customers, not seeing my staff, not even my husband when he gets home. I used to love planning the seasonal menus, but now I can’t decide on anything. Even picking what to wear in the morning feels overwhelming—I stand there staring at my clothes like they’re written in another language.  

I’ve lost so much energy. Opening the restaurant, which used to be second nature, takes everything out of me. I’ll sit in the office between rushes and just feel paralyzed, like my body won’t listen. My staff has noticed I’m quieter, less present. I canceled dinner with friends twice last month—I didn’t want to be rude, but the thought of making small talk drained me before I even left the house.

This has been going on for about ten months. I can’t say there was one big thing that started it. The pandemic slowed us down, staffing has been tough, and my dad’s health has been shaky—but nothing that hasn’t passed before. I’m still running the place, still showing up, but it’s like I’m watching myself do it from a distance. I don’t know if this is stress, sadness, or something more—nothing feels clear anymore.
D013-D020_h011.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D020_h011.answer: C & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about ten months now—just a steady heaviness, like I’m moving through fog. Some days I can’t get out of bed until late morning, even if I’ve slept. I used to love working on design projects—there was something satisfying about turning an idea into a space people could live in—but now, even when I finish a presentation or win a client’s approval, it feels… empty. It doesn’t stick.  

I’m exhausted all the time. I’ll nap after work and still feel drained. My focus is shot, too—I keep misplacing my keys, forgetting where I saved files, missing deadlines I used to handle easily. It’s starting to show at work. I’ve had to ask colleagues to double-check my drawings because I’m scared I’ve made mistakes.  

Things have been hard lately—my dad got sick last year, my lease ended, and I’ve been managing everything alone. I don’t know if that’s why I feel this way or if it would’ve happened anyway. I wouldn’t say I’m *overwhelmed* by it all, but it’s always there, like background noise. I just don’t feel like myself anymore.
D013-D020_h012.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D020_h012.answer: C & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about ten months now—maybe a little over. Some days it’s like I’m moving through fog. I wake up already tired, even if I slept okay, and my mind feels sluggish, like I can’t quite grasp what I’m reading or follow a conversation without having to replay it in my head. I teach from home—tutor high school kids in English—and honestly, I’ve had to reschedule sessions because I just can’t focus. Getting started on lesson plans takes so much effort, even though I used to enjoy it.  

I wouldn’t say I’m crying all the time, but I feel… heavy. Like joy doesn’t land the same. I stopped calling friends. My daughter notices. I love her, but motivating myself to do things—even small stuff like cooking or going out—feels overwhelming.  

I did go through a rough patch last year—my divorce finalized around then, money’s been tight with fewer students lately. I don’t know if that’s still affecting me or if this is something else. I can’t tell if I’m just stuck in a bad stretch or if this is more than that. Some weeks are better, but not enough to feel normal again.
D013-D020_h013.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D020_h013.answer: C & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h014.question: Lately, I’ve just been… off. It’s been nearly a year now—maybe ten months—where I wake up already exhausted, like I’m dragging through wet concrete. I run a tough job—mergers and acquisitions—so stress isn’t new, but this feels different. I used to thrive under pressure. Now, I skip client dinners, ignore calls from friends, even my daughter has noticed I’m “checked out.” I don’t hate life, exactly, but I don’t feel much in it either. I miss meetings with colleagues I once enjoyed. I forget details—simple stuff, like where I put my laptop or what time calls were scheduled. I tell myself it’s just being busy, but it’s not like me. After my divorce two years ago, I kept it together—work didn't suffer. But lately, I’ve had to reschedule pitches. I sit in my apartment at night, staring at the walls, not watching TV, not reading. I don’t feel suicidal or hopeless in a dramatic way—just numb, tired, like the volume’s been turned down on everything. I can’t tell if this is just a rough patch, a reaction to everything piling up, or if it’s something more. Some days I feel okay—almost normal—so I wonder, is it really that bad?

A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h015.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about ten months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. I wake up already exhausted, and no amount of sleep fixes it. I used to find real satisfaction in closing a tough deal, but now, even when I do, there’s just… nothing. No pride, no buzz. My kids took me to a baseball game last weekend—just wanted to spend time together—and I started tearing up during the national anthem. I barely made it through without excusing myself. That’s been happening more: out of nowhere, I’ll get overwhelmed and just cry, even at stupid things—commercials, a tone in someone’s voice.  

Decisions are torture now. I’ll stand in front of the fridge for ten minutes trying to pick a yogurt. In meetings, I second-guess every recommendation. Used to be sharp, fast—now I feel foggy. I thought it was the divorce at first—still do, part of me—everything fell apart a year ago. But I keep wondering: is this just how you fall apart slowly when your life changes, or is it more than that? I go to work, I function, but I’m not really *there*. I don’t know if I need healing or a diagnosis.
D013-D020_h015.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D020_h015.answer: C & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h016.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—maybe a year and a half. It started around the time I moved cities to focus on freelance work, but honestly, it’s hard to pin it to one thing. The past few months especially, I just don’t feel any joy in stuff I used to love, like editing music videos or going out with friends. It’s not that I’m sad all the time—I wouldn’t say I’m crying every day or anything—but everything feels flat, like I’m just going through the motions.

Falling asleep takes forever. My mind just races, even when I’m exhausted. And during the day, I move slowly—like I have to remind myself to stand up, grab my laptop, answer emails. Clients have asked if I’m sick because I’ve been turning in work late, and I hate that I’m letting them down. I keep thinking I’m not good enough, that I’m just... wasting time.

A few things have been stressful—freelancing is unstable, and I’ve been lonely since the move—but I don’t know if that explains everything. Some weeks I feel a bit better, others it all crashes back. I wouldn’t say things are completely falling apart, but it’s definitely affecting my life.
D013-D020_h016.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D013-D020_h016.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h017.question:
I’ve just turned 33, and honestly, I don’t feel like I’m getting anywhere. I used to care—about my edits, about landing better projects—but now it’s like nothing matters, even when people compliment my work. I remember winning an award last year, but it didn’t move me. I just felt… empty.  

Falling asleep’s been tough. I lie there for hours, mind racing, but not about anything real—just these strange, heavy thoughts. Like I caused that car accident downtown last winter, even though I wasn’t anywhere near it. Or that my silence on a group chat somehow ruined a friend’s relationship. It doesn’t make sense, I know, but the guilt sticks like glue.  

I notice myself moving slower now—grabbing coffee, zipping my jacket, even typing. My assistant asked if I was hurt. I’m not, just… heavy. It takes effort to do basic things, and editing, which used to flow, now takes twice as long. I’m behind on cuts, but I can’t seem to care enough to fix it.  

This has been going on for over a year—maybe a year and a half. There was some stress around my dad’s illness, and money’s been tight, but I don’t know if that’s really "the" reason. Things just… darkened.
D013-D020_h017.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D013-D020_h018.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—maybe a year and a half. It started slowly, I guess, and I didn’t think much of it at first. At the zoo, I used to love the morning routines—the feeding, the cleaning, checking on the animals. Now, I make it through the motions, but it takes everything just to get out of the truck. I walk slower than I used to; my coworkers have even asked if I’m hurt. I’m not—I just feel heavy.

Sleep’s been patchy. I wake up around 3 or 4 most nights and just lie there, staring. By morning, I’m wiped. It’s hard to start the day. Even small things feel like they require too much effort. Some days I don’t want to come in at all.

I’ve been feeling... responsible, somehow, for things that aren’t really on me. Last week one of the primates got sick, nothing serious, but I kept thinking it was because I missed a detail in his diet log. I know that’s not fair—but still, it sits on me. My wife’s been patient, but I hate seeing the look in her eyes when I don’t respond. I want to be better, but I’m stuck. There was some stress at home last year—a financial scare, nothing we couldn’t handle—but I don’t know if that’s really *why* I feel like this. It just won’t lift.
D013-D020_h018.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D013-D020_h018.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h019.question:
I’ve just turned 45 this year, and even though things look fine on the outside—my husband and I are still together, I’ve been principal at the same high school for over a decade—I feel… stuck. Like I’m moving through thick fog. It started gradually, maybe a year and a half ago, but I can’t pinpoint exactly when. I used to love gardening—spent weekends planting, pruning—but now I just don’t care. I’ll look at the overgrown backyard and feel guilty, like I’m failing my home, failing *him*… over something so stupid, but it sticks to me.  

Sleep’s no better. I go to bed early, wake up after eight hours, and still feel like I haven’t slept at all. I drag myself through the day, and even small tasks—signing papers, walking to the next classroom—take forever. My staff have asked if I’m okay more than once.  

What bothers me most is this constant weight, like I’ve done something wrong, even when I haven’t. I replay routine decisions at school—scheduling a meeting, sending an email—and think, *I shouldn’t have done that. I’ve ruined something.* It doesn’t make sense, but it won’t let go.  

Something shifted around that time… maybe stress at home? Work? I don’t know. But it’s not like one thing caused it—it just seeped in.
D013-D020_h019.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D013-D020_h019.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—maybe a year and a half. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when it started because things have always been kind of chaotic with my job. I tour with a band, so my schedule’s irregular, but even by those standards, I’ve been struggling. I wake up around 4 or 5 most mornings, completely exhausted, but my mind’s racing and I can’t get back to sleep. I end up pacing the hotel room or picking at my hands until they’re raw.  

It’s not that I don’t care about the job—I still show up, I get the cues right—but everything feels heavier. I have to talk myself through each task like I’m climbing a hill. There’s this constant loop in my head, going over tiny mistakes: that time I missed a cue in Portland, something I said to a coworker months ago that might’ve sounded sharp. I replay it and beat myself up, even though rationally I know it wasn’t a big deal.  

Things at home haven’t been easy either—my dad’s been ill, and I’ve been the one managing stuff from the road. I don’t know if that’s why I feel this way or if it would’ve happened anyway. I haven’t told anyone until now.
D013-D020_h020.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D013-D020_h020.answer: C & B. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—maybe a year and a half. It started subtly, like a weight slowly pressing down. Most days I feel… hollow, like nothing matters. I don’t cry much, but the sadness is just *there*, like a constant hum in the background. I used to run every morning—standard for us officers—but now I can’t even decide what to wear, let alone face the day. Picking a meal, choosing gear for training… simple things feel overwhelming, and I second-guess everything.  

Sleep’s the worst. I keep having the same nightmare—my unit pinned down, me unable to call in support. I wake up drenched, heart racing, sometimes screaming. I haven’t been able to talk about it. A few months ago, after a particularly bad night, I filled a bottle with extra painkillers I had from an old injury. I didn’t take them, but… I kept them by my bed for weeks. Didn’t throw them out until a buddy noticed.  

We’ve had back-to-back deployments, and my chain of command has noticed the slip—delayed reports, missed briefings. I don’t know if it’s just the stress of command, or something deeper. I tell myself I should be able to handle it, but I don’t feel like I can anymore.
D013-D020_h021.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D013-D020_h021.answer: B & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D013-D020_h022.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—just feeling… hollow. Like I’m going through the motions, especially with work. I shoot weddings, you know, all these big, joyful moments, and I’m supposed to feel excited, present, but I just feel numb. It’s like I’m watching everything from behind glass.  

Falling asleep has become this huge battle. I lie there for hours, my mind either blank or spinning in circles. I can’t think clearly anymore—it’s hard to make simple decisions, even picking out what to wear or what music to use in a slideshow. Everything feels foggy, like I’m dragging myself through mud.  

There are times—honestly—when I think about not being here. Not because I want to hurt myself in a violent way, but because I imagine a specific moment: maybe driving out somewhere quiet, turning off the car, and just… not waking up. It feels like an escape from the weight.  

My husband notices. I’ve pulled away. Missed a few gigs. But I can’t say it’s because of one big thing—it didn’t start after a single event. It just… seeped in. I don’t know if this is depression, or just life, or me failing to cope.
